semantic_correction.stem: A client has a chest tube connected to a water-seal drainage system. During repositioning, the patient-side tubing becomes disconnected from the drainage unit; the tube remains secured in the client's chest, and the client has no new respiratory distress. A replacement system is being brought. The facility emergency chest-tube protocol permits use of sterile water as a temporary water seal when this disconnection occurs. Which action is most appropriate while awaiting the replacement system?

options.A: Clamp the chest tube near the insertion site and leave it clamped until a replacement drainage system is available and connected.
options.B: Place the disconnected distal tubing in sterile water per the emergency protocol to create a temporary water seal while help brings a new system.
options.C: Reconnect the separated tubing to the existing drainage unit immediately without replacing or evaluating the disconnected components for contamination.
options.D: Raise the open distal tubing above the level of the client's chest and wait for the replacement system while continuing respiratory assessment.

semantic_correction.rationale: The 2026 NCSBN NCLEX-RN Test Plan explicitly requires newly licensed RNs to monitor and maintain devices and equipment used for drainage, including chest-tube suction systems, under Physiological Adaptation. Open RN/NCBI guidance for accidental disconnection of chest-tube tubing from the drainage system recommends obtaining assistance to replace the drainage system and describes a temporary water seal using sterile water as an option while the system is being restored. The stem deliberately supplies the facility-specific protocol authorizing this temporary measure. B is therefore the uniquely best action while the replacement system is being obtained. A leaves the chest tube clamped rather than using the stated temporary water-seal protocol and can obstruct pleural drainage. C reconnects potentially contaminated/disrupted components without proper evaluation or replacement. D leaves the patient-side tubing open rather than restoring a one-way water-seal pathway. Therefore B is correct.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: When chest-tube tubing becomes disconnected from the drainage system, protect the client from loss of the drainage/water-seal pathway, obtain help to replace the system, and use the facility-approved temporary water-seal method when indicated rather than leaving the tube open or continuously clamped.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: retired preceptor/transition-to-practice research trivia because it did not test a bedside entry-level nursing action. Rebuilt the item around explicit NCSBN chest-tube drainage-device management. The stem controls the facility's emergency protocol to avoid universalizing a single implementation and removes the prior absolute-word cue.

scope_exclusions.universal_temporary_water_seal_rule: Not asserted. The stem explicitly states that the facility emergency protocol permits sterile-water temporary sealing for this disconnection scenario.
scope_exclusions.chest_tube_dislodged_from_patient: Not tested. The tube remains secured in the client's chest; only the tubing-to-drainage-system connection is disrupted.
scope_exclusions.prolonged_clamping: Not endorsed. The item avoids leaving the tube continuously clamped while a replacement system is obtained.
scope_exclusions.active_respiratory_deterioration: Not present in the stem. If new distress or vital-sign deterioration developed, immediate assessment/escalation would take priority alongside restoration of the drainage system.

near_duplicate_check.note: V2-Q0724 tests rapid-response activation for acute postoperative deterioration. V2-Q0622 tests malfunctioning infusion-pump removal/reporting. V2-Q0676 tests a smoking ignition source near prescribed oxygen. V2-Q0971 tests accidental disconnection of a chest-tube drainage system and temporary restoration of the water-seal pathway. Targeted repository search returned no matching chest-tube disconnection item before staging.

option_audit.A: Plausible emergency maneuver but leaves the chest tube clamped continuously rather than using the facility-authorized temporary water-seal pathway.
option_audit.B: Correct. It follows the supplied emergency protocol to restore a temporary water seal while a replacement system is obtained.
option_audit.C: Plausible rapid reconnection response but bypasses evaluation/replacement of disrupted potentially contaminated components.
option_audit.D: Plausible attempt to prevent backflow but leaves the patient-side tubing open rather than restoring the drainage water seal.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible best answer under the controlled stem. The facility protocol explicitly permits a sterile-water temporary seal and the tube remains in the client. B alone restores the temporary one-way water-seal pathway while help brings a replacement. A leaves the tube clamped, C bypasses safe system replacement/evaluation, and D leaves the tubing open.

cueing_check.note: Correct option B is not longest and is close in length to C/D; all choices are parallel action responses without absolute-word traps.
